The image shows a mango leaf with dark, sooty, irregular black deposits scattered across the surface. The leaf remains mostly green with black powdery/crusty patches distributed over the lamina — no necrotic lesions, no tip dieback, no white powdery growth, and no sunken anthracnose spots.

This pattern — dark black sooty coating on the leaf surface — is characteristic of Sooty Mould, caused by fungi growing on honeydew secreted by insects.
